excluded_candidates.reason: Seven direct PubMed title/abstract records existed by 2015.

eligible_results.assessment: A KRAS-mutant CT26 mouse colorectal cancer model experimentally tested MEK inhibition with anti-CTLA-4 and found sequence-dependent enhancement. This supports treatment-response relevance, but does not prove that KRAS status itself causally controls CTLA-4 response.

Later human observational studies directly examined the pair, but did not test the proposed dysbiosis chain; one large cross-sectional study found less, not more, moderate periodontal bone loss in celiac disease.

interpretation: The workflow is technically feasible and generated temporally novel links, but this two-candidate feasibility sample does not meet a 70-80% strict experimental-validation target and cannot establish superiority over Traditional RAG.
